case_name: Samghaji Hariba Patil v State of Karnataka
respondent:
State of Karnataka
Supreme Court of India

19 October 2006
Appeal (Cr.) 444 of 2006
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
1.  This appeal u/s. 2 of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970 arises out of a judgment and order dated 16th September, 2005 passed by the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore in Criminal Appeal No.936 of 1999 whereby and where under an appeal preferred by the State of Karnataka against a judgment and order of acquittal passed by the trial court was allowed.
2.  Appellant herein along with three
facts: The appeal arises out of a judgment and order dated 16th September, 2005 passed by the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore.
Appellant herein along with three others was accused of commission of an offence punishable under Sections 302, 307, 504 read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'IPC').
The deceased and the accused No.1 Ningappa Bhaganna Padagaon belonged to the same village.
P.W.2 his son, Bhaganna, P.W.3 his wife, Tangawwa and P.W.4 his daughter, Mayavva, were said to be present at that place.
The incident is said to have been witnessed by some of the independent witnesses.
There were many houses around the land in question.
P.W.2 and other witnesses admitted that there were 30 to 40 houses sounding the agricultural land where the incident allegedly occurred.
issues: Whether the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt?
Whether the trial court's judgment of acquittal was correct?
Whether the High Court's reversal of the trial court's judgment was justified?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant did not have any land in the vicinity.
There exists a dispute as to whether the land where allegedly the occurrence took place belonged to the deceased.
The accused No.1, admittedly, did not own any bullocks to plough his land.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution had been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The trial court's judgment of acquittal was incorrect.
The High Court's reversal of the trial court's judgment was justified.
court_reasoning: The learned Trial Judge noticed various discrepancies in recording its judgment of acquittal.
The learned Judge opined that the prosecution had not been able to prove its case.
The High Court relied upon the testimonies of the so-called eye witnesses and reversed the said judgment.
holding: The appeal preferred by the State of Karnataka against a judgment and order of acquittal passed by the trial court was allowed.
The High Court set aside the said judgment and order, convicting the appellant herein for commission of an offence u/s.302 IPC.
